svg.text: N is greyed out — the auto-indexing input tunnel sets it
INNER FOR LOOP N = 4 cells per frame
CASE STRUCTURE — TRUE (log frames? is ON)
FALSE: one straight error wire, input tunnel → output tunnel
THREE KINDS OF TUNNEL, AND THE DIFFERENCE MATTERS. The bracketed [ ] tunnels auto-index:
one element in or out per iteration. TL1 auto-indexes IN, so it also sets N — that is why the
outer loop’s N terminal is greyed and unwired. TL2 is a PLAIN tunnel: the same 16-character
payload string is handed to every one of the 4 inner iterations, not sliced up.
TR1b is the CONCATENATING tunnel — the odd one out. The inner loop hands it a 4-element array
each pass; concatenating joins them end to end into ONE 96-element array. Leave it auto-indexing
and you get a 24 × 4 two-dimensional array instead, and Judge_OCV.vi will refuse to wire up.
Right-click the tunnel ▸ Tunnel Mode ▸ Concatenating. It is one menu item and it is the whole VI.
The frame-order check: the loop counter i plus 800 (0x320) must equal the CAN ID decoded from
the frame. And Array Elements turns 24 booleans into one verdict. If frames arrive out of order
the voltages land on the wrong cells and every number downstream is quietly wrong.
The 1000 constant feeding Divide must be ORANGE. Type it into a blue integer constant and you get
integer division: 3738/1000 = 3, and all 96 cells read 3.000. Right-click ▸ Representation ▸ DBL.
Note the error wire: DUT_Query’s error out goes to the Case Structure, and Close File’s error out
comes back out of it. Logging is an option; measuring is not. Unwired terminals — format string,
offset, default, trace?, elapsed ms, coerced(x), offset past number — keep their defaults.
FALSE case: input tunnel wired straight across to output tunnel, nothing else
